params.body:
The question was whether people use the platform more since the migration. The obvious answer was an nginx access log, and it turned out to be the wrong one twice over: it is switched off in the Forge config and needs root to change, and it keeps the IP of every visitor — on a dealer's public website, the personal data of our customers' customers. It also knows a url where the application knows which garage and which screen.

So the counting happens in the application instead.

## A daily total, not a row per view

One row per (day, person, screen) with a counter. That answers every question the screen asks — how many views, how many people, how many garages, which screens — at a few hundred rows a day instead of hundreds of thousands a month. A row per view would have been the lazy shape for a number nobody reads at that resolution.

`INSERT ... ON DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE`, not read-then-write: two tabs opened in the same second would both read the same number and both write it back, and the count would quietly run behind.

## Four filters, each for its own reason

Counting happens **after** the response, and only for a signed-in user, a `GET`, a named route and a 200.

- After, because a page that failed is not a page that was read — and because the write does not belong in front of the thing the dealer is waiting for.
- `GET`, because a Livewire update is a POST to its own endpoint; counting those turns one screen into fifty views while somebody types in a filter, and the busiest screen becomes whichever one has the most live fields.
- A named route, because a path carries ids and every row would be unique.

## What it cannot see, and says so

Visitors who are not signed in. Somebody browsing a dealer's public website without an account is not counted, and the screen prints that rather than letting a reader assume the number covers everyone. No IP address is kept anywhere.

Like the event log, this starts empty, so it sits in its own block with the date it started and is never added to the handlings.

## Verified

Seven tests: a second view raises the counter instead of adding a row, another screen is its own row, nothing is counted without a signed-in person, a Livewire update is not a page view, opening a screen counts it through the middleware, an unwritable counter does not break the page, and the screens carry the people behind them (a screen opened a thousand times by one person is a different fact from one opened a thousand times by eighty).

`phpstan` green over the project, `pint` green on the added files. `Kernel.php` and the Livewire component are touched by four and three added lines; no reformatting.

Local suite: the same nine failures as on a clean `main` in my environment (two known `ListPageHeadersTest`, six `IntegrationSmokeTest` that read an `OUTBOUND_IMPACT` from my local `.env`, and one warranty test). My local database is still carrying rows an earlier test of mine leaked through DDL; CI runs on a fresh database.

New rule R P3-16.9.
params.title: Counting pages without counting people
